facts.text: The DMV gives a vision test to all applicants to make sure they can see well enough to drive safely.

cites.quote: DMV tests all applicants to ensure they can see well enough to drive safely.

facts.text: If you take the vision test wearing corrective or contact lenses, your driver's license will have a corrective lenses restriction.

cites.quote: If you take your vision test with corrective or contact lenses, your driver’s license will have a corrective lenses restriction.

facts.text: If you do not pass the DMV vision test, you will be asked to have your eye doctor complete a Report of Vision Examination (DL 62) form.

cites.quote: If you do not pass your vision test, you will be asked to have your eye doctor complete a Report of Vision Examination (DL 62) form.

facts.text: For an original driver's license, you must pass a multiple-choice knowledge test.

cites.quote: When you apply for an original driver’s license, you must pass a knowledge test with multiple choice questions.

facts.text: You get three attempts to pass the knowledge test before you must reapply.

cites.quote: You are allowed three attempts to pass before you must reapply.

facts.text: A minor who fails the knowledge test must wait seven days to retake it, not counting the day of the failure.

cites.quote: Minors must wait seven days to retake a failed knowledge test, not including the day of the failure.

facts.text: When renewing a driver's license, eLearning (a no-fail, self-paced course with quizzes after each module) may be an alternative to the knowledge test.

cites.quote: When renewing your driver’s license, eLearning may be an alternative testing option. This is a no-fail, self-paced interactive modulated course with quizzes after each module.

facts.text: You may not use any testing aids, such as the California Driver's Handbook or a cell phone, during a knowledge test.

cites.quote: You are not allowed to use any testing aids during knowledge tests, such as a California Driver’s Handbook or cell phone.

facts.text: When you apply for an original driver's license, you are tested on your ability to drive a vehicle safely in a behind-the-wheel drive test.

cites.quote: When you apply for an original driver’s license, you will be tested on your ability to safely drive a vehicle.

facts.text: When renewing, drivers with a vision or medical condition may be required to take a behind-the-wheel test.

cites.quote: Upon renewal, drivers with a vision or medical condition may be required to take a behind-the-wheel test.

facts.text: During the drive test, the examiner may give two or more instructions at once to see whether you can understand and follow both.

cites.quote: The examiner may give two or more instructions at one time to determine whether you can understand and properly follow both directions.

facts.text: On the day of your behind-the-wheel test, you must bring your instruction permit or driver's license, if you have one.

cites.quote: On the day of your behind-the-wheel test, you must bring:
Your instruction permit or driver’s license (if you have one).

facts.text: Unless you are already licensed, you must bring another California-licensed driver at least 18 years old (25 for minors) to your behind-the-wheel test.

cites.quote: On the day of your behind-the-wheel test, you must bring:
Another California-licensed driver who is at least 18 years old (25 for minors), unless you are already licensed to drive.

facts.text: You must bring a vehicle that is safe to drive to your behind-the-wheel test.

cites.quote: On the day of your behind-the-wheel test, you must bring:
A vehicle that is safe to drive for your test.

facts.text: You must bring valid proof of insurance and vehicle registration to your behind-the-wheel test.

cites.quote: On the day of your behind-the-wheel test, you must bring:
Valid proof of insurance and vehicle registration.

facts.text: If you use a rental vehicle for your drive test, your name must be on the rental contract and the contract must not exclude behind-the-wheel drive tests.

cites.quote: If you plan to use a rental vehicle for your drive test, your name must be listed on the rental contract. The contract must not exclude behind-the-wheel drive tests.

facts.text: A minor who fails the behind-the-wheel drive test must wait 14 days to retake it, not counting the day of the failure.

cites.quote: Minors must wait 14 days to retake a failed behind-the-wheel drive test, not including the day of the failure.

facts.text: For the drive test, the window on the driver's side of your vehicle must open.

cites.quote: Before you begin, the DMV examiner will ask you to locate and demonstrate the following:
The window on the driver side must open.

facts.text: For the drive test, the windshield must give you and the examiner a full, clear, unblocked view; windshield cracks may postpone your test.

cites.quote: The windshield must allow a full, clear, unblocked view for you and the DMV examiner. Windshield cracks may postpone your test.

facts.text: For the drive test, your vehicle must have at least two rearview mirrors, one of them on the left side.

cites.quote: At least two rearview mirrors. One of them must be on the left side of your vehicle.

facts.text: For the drive test, both the right and left brake lights must work.

cites.quote: The right and left brake lights must be operational.

facts.text: For the drive test, your tires must have at least 1/32-inch of uniform tread depth.

cites.quote: The tires must have at least 1/32-inch of uniformed tread depth.

facts.text: A donut (spare) tire may not be used during a drive test.

cites.quote: The use of a donut tire is not allowed during a drive test.

facts.text: For the drive test, there must be at least one inch of clearance between the bottom of the pressed brake pedal and the floorboard.

cites.quote: There must be at least one inch of clearance between the bottom of the brake pedal and the floorboard when depressed.

facts.text: For the drive test, the horn must be designed for the vehicle, work properly, and be loud enough to be heard from at least 200 feet.

cites.quote: Designed for the vehicle, in proper working condition, and loud enough to be heard from a distance of at least 200 feet.

facts.text: Before the drive test, the examiner will ask you to show how to set and release the parking brake.

cites.quote: Before you begin, the DMV examiner will ask you to locate and demonstrate the following:
How to set and release the parking brake.

facts.text: Before the drive test, the examiner will ask you to demonstrate the turn/arm signals for a left turn, a right turn, and slowing down or stopping.

cites.quote: Before you begin, the DMV examiner will ask you to locate and demonstrate the following:
Left turn.
Right turn.
Slowing down or stopping.

facts.text: Before the drive test, you may be required to show that your windshield wipers work.

cites.quote: You may be required to show they function.

facts.text: For the drive test, all seat belts must work properly and be used by everyone in the vehicle.

cites.quote: All seat belts must work properly and be used by the individual(s) in the vehicle.

facts.text: If your vehicle does not meet the drive test requirements, your drive test will be rescheduled.

cites.quote: If your vehicle does not meet the requirements, your drive test will be rescheduled.

facts.text: Interpreters may help during the pre-drive inspection but may not ride with you during the drive test.

cites.quote: Interpreters may be used during the pre-drive inspection for the identification and use of certain controls in the vehicle but may not accompany you during the drive test.

facts.text: Only the examiner may accompany you during the drive test, except for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

cites.quote: Only the examiner is allowed to accompany you during the drive test. Exceptions are made for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

facts.text: Using a recording device (video or audio) during a behind-the-wheel drive test is prohibited; if it cannot be turned off, you must block it.

cites.quote: The use of a recording device, including a video/audio recorder, is prohibited during a behind-the-wheel drive test.
If the recording device cannot be powered off or disabled, the applicant must block it

facts.text: Advanced driver assistance systems such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control are not permitted during the drive test.

cites.quote: advanced driver assistance systems technologies, such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control, are not permitted during the drive test.

facts.text: Backup cameras and blind spot monitors may be used on the drive test, but they do not replace visually checking your mirrors and blind spots.

cites.quote: Vehicle safety technology, such as backup cameras and blind spot monitors, may be used on the drive test, but are not a replacement for an actual visual check of your mirrors and blind spots.
